takeaway: Inguinal canal roof: internal oblique, conjoint tendon and transversus abdominis. Front: external oblique aponeurosis (internal oblique laterally). Back: transversalis fascia (conjoint tendon medially). Floor: inguinal, lacunar ligaments.

lines.text: The inguinal canal is an oblique 4–6 cm slit above the medial half of the inguinal ligament.
lines.say: The inguinal canal is an oblique four to six centimetre slit above the medial half of the inguinal ligament.

lines.text: Its roof is made of three structures: internal oblique, the conjoint tendon and transversus abdominis.
In front: the external oblique aponeurosis, reinforced laterally by internal oblique.
Behind: the transversalis fascia, reinforced medially by the conjoint tendon.
And the floor: the inguinal and lacunar ligaments.
Together, these boundaries reduce this natural point of weakness.
So the roof is internal oblique, conjoint tendon and transversus abdominis.
lines.say: (clears throat) So the roof is internal oblique, conjoint tendon and transversus abdominis.
